previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections presented with nausea, vomiting, and fever. She developed septic shock with hypotension and hyperkalemia, requiring ICU admission. Initial broad-spectrum antibiotics were given, later de-escalated to ciprofloxacin after urine culture identified Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to ciprofloxacin. Her acute kidney injury, attributed to pre-renal causes from hypovolemia, improved with intravenous fluids. A central line was placed for antibiotic access and later removed. She was discharged home on oral ciprofloxacin with stable vital signs and improved renal function, with follow-up planned with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old diabetic female with chief complaint of fever, 
pyuria, and leukocytosis w/ LLE cellulitis growing GNR/Staph 
aureus complicated by recurrent C. diff.
.
ACTIVE ISSUES
-------------
# Left lower extremity cellulitis - patient is status post stump 
revision. Tissue culture grew gram negative rods and Staph 
aureus.  The patient presented with mild warmth of the left 
stump with associated edema.  Infectious disease was consulted 
and recommended vancomycin treatment for seven days, which was 
completed while the patient was hospitalized.
.
# Left knee osteomyelitis: due to patient's cellulitis, X-ray of 
the left lower stump was obtained and findings suggested 
osteomyelitis.  MRI was then obtained which was inconclusive for 
osteomyelitis.  Patient underwent revision her left lower 
extremity stump, upon which bone samples were obtained and 
culture results grew out gram negative rods, including 
Klebsiella and E.coli.  The patient was initiated on tigecycline 
pre-procedure, which was continued when osteomyelitis was 
concerned.  At this time, not all sensitivities have returned on 
the organisms cultured.  Patient was discharged on IV 
tigecycline for a proposed six week course, with close follow-up 
scheduled with Infectious Disease, where the antibiotic regimen 
will be altered as needed based on further culture results.  
.
# Acute kidney injury - patient's creatinine was elevated at 
times during her hospitalization above her baseline of 1.7. This 
was thought to be due to pre-renal physiology, given response to 
IV fluids.  Creatinine level on discharge was 1.9.  Patient was 
continued on her home dose of Nephrocaps.  Nephrotoxins were 
avoided and medications were renally dosed.
.
# Urinary tract infection: patient was noted to have urine 
culture that grew >100,000 E.coli during her hospitalization.  
She was treated with a course of ampicillin, which was ceased 
when she was started on tigecycline for osteomyelitis.  Patient 
self-catheterizes herself at home, and patient was instructed on 
how to do this before leaving the hospital, and how to do this 
in the most sterile environment possible.
.
# Peripheral arterial disease: patient underwent left lower 
extremity stump revision during her hospitalization without 
event.  She will follow up with Vascular Surgery upon discharge.
.
INACTIVE ISSUES
---------------
# Clostridium difficile infection: patient has a history of C. 
difficile infection.  Towards the end of her hospital course, 
patient had diarrhea concerning for recurrence of C. difficile 
infection after a course of ampicillin and vancomycin during her 
hospitalization.  Per Infectious Disease recommendations, the 
pateint was started on Vancomycin orally.  Stool toxin assay was 
checked and was negative x 1. Vancomycin was ceased upon 
negative toxin assay result.
.
# Type I diabetes mellitus:  blood sugars were relatively 
well-controlled over ___ hospital course.  She was 
continued on her home regimen of Lantus and sliding scale 
humalog.  She was also continued on her home dose of aspirin.   
.
# Depression: symptoms were stable. No suicidal ideation was 
present.  Patient was continued on her home dose of citalopram.
.  
TRANSITION OF CARE
------------------
# Follow-up: patient has pending bone tissue cultures at the 
time of discharge, which will need to be followed up.  She is 
currently receiving IV tigecycline through a ___ line for a 
proposed six week course.  She will have follow up with her 
primary care provider, ___ and Infectious Disease.  
Patient was also noted to be hypertensive towards the end of her 
hospital course, which should be followed up as well.
.  
# Code status: full code, confirmed
.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Diabetes, BKA stump infection, six months' postop from BKA,

COMPARISON:  Radiographs from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar non-contrast images of the left calf, and BKA stump
were acquired on a 1.5 Tesla magnet per department protocol.

FINDINGS:  The patient is status post below-knee amputation.  There is
relatively thin area of soft tissue overlying the distal aspect of the stump,
and there are foci of susceptibility artifact seen in the distal soft tissues
(7, 13 and 8, 13), which likely represent postoperative change.  Edema is seen

superficial posterior compartment (6, 20), though scattered areas of edema are
seen throughout.  There is no fluid collection, or other sign of abscess.

No definite marrow signal abnormality is evident.  There is periosteal
thickening and remodeling at the anterior aspect of the distal fibula (7, 19),
though no definite signal change is seen within the bone itself.

This study was not specifically tailored for evaluation of internal
derangement within the knee.  No definite knee joint abnormality is seen.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Nonspecific signal changes in the soft tissues surrounding the distal
aspect of the stump, that could represent cellulitis and/or myositis in the
appropriate clinical setting.  
2.  No definite evidence of osteomyelitis.  Small area of periosteal reaction
and bony remodeling about the distal fibula, could relate to altered
weightbearing or chronic stress.
